title: The Holland album with Ted Easton's jazz band
summary: She stayed after the tour to record in a studio with Ted Easton, felt stranded, and sang songs from copies in her case.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe

blocks.x: The next thing from '75 is the record we mentioned before which was recorded in Holland with Ted Easton.
Yeah. As I said before, we had worked at the New Orleans Club -- Ted Easton, that's his club. And --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Now the place name on this is -- I guess you'd say it's Scheveningen. Yeah?
Yeah, whatever that means.
However. But that's just outside Amsterdam.
I think it's outside The Hague.
Okay.
Yeah, I think that's where it is. And as I said before, we had worked at Ted's club the night before.
He's an ex-patriot American, isn't he?

Yes. He has his own club, and I think he does a little promoting. I think he bring a lot of American artists over there. He mentioned the fact that he had caught the Carnegie Hall concert. And he liked 'I've Got The World On A String.'
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

So, he asked me if I'd stay over and do an album, which I did. We got up that next morning and the band took the bus to the next gig, and left me standing out in front of the hotel waiting for Ted Easton to show up so we could make this album.
I felt very, very much stranded at that particular point, because Ted was a little late showing up, and I got a little nervous, because I didn't know what I was going to do next.
But he finally showed up and we made the album in a studio there with his musicians.
And I happened to have some extra copies of music in my case -- you know, things that I don't necessarily do in repertoire, but like some spares.
And so we got a chance to do -- In fact, -- let's see, one, two, three, four, five, six -- six of the songs are songs that I had never recorded before.
Yeah.
'The Lady's In Love With You,' 'On The Sunny Side Of The Street,' 'I Cover The
Waterfront," "Some Day Sweetheart," "I Surrender Dear," and "Something To Remember You By."
You know, there was no piano on this -- in the orchestra.
That's right.
And also, it has a dixieland front line, but it's not atall a dixieland sounding group.
No.
The band features mostly all of the things that Louie Armstrong ever did. I mean, they really imitate the band and most of his selections as much as they can.
The guitar player is a very talented musician, because although I had lead sheets on most of these things, he had to sort of scribble out the progressions for the other instruments.
And he did it without even looking at the music. He had a terrific ear and he's a very good guitar player.
After we did the session, I went to the airport and he was at the airport. He was getting ready to go to Spain. He was on holiday and he
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

was getting ready to go to Spain, so I got a chance to see him again. And, of course, I took a plane and I joined the band immediately. I don't know exactly where we went. We probably were on our way to Denmark. Yeah, I think I joined them in Copenhagen.
And pretty shortly thereafter, you were on your way to Sweden.
Yes.
Where you did your next pair of records.
Yes.
You have anything more to say about this?
No, no. That's all I have to say about this.
Okay.
I can't pronounce these guys' names. We'll let that lay where it is.
